title: Understanding Automated Program Repair Agents through the Lens of Traceability: An Empirical Study
read_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.08311v3 (author full text; published as PACMSE 3, ISSTA 2026; DOI 10.1145/3832285)
datasets: SWE-bench Verified, 500 Python issue tasks across 12 repositories; primary trace collection is 500 task instances. Also uses Verified-50 random subset for manual analysis and new reproducer generation/localization experiments.

Public Hugging Face dataset `zt6c3mxv8q/logs_and_trajs`: 3.28 GB trajectory/log repository documented to include agent predictions, metadata, trajectories, logs and results. Models/agent combinations include Agentless, AutoCodeRover, MASAI, SWE-Agent and OpenHands with Claude-3.5-Sonnet/GPT-4o (some combinations unavailable).
SWT-Bench/SWT-Bench-Lite appears in related work only; not used as the experimental benchmark.
task: Trace-based empirical comparison of five workflow/open-process APR agents across patch similarity to developers, resolution by issue difficulty, issue-reproducer generation, patch overfitting, regression-test selection and tool use. RQ3 additionally tests whether bug-localization context improves generated reproducer tests.
input_setting: Issue report + buggy repository snapshot from SWE-bench Verified; agents generate patches and sometimes reproducer/regression tests. Reproducer study varies Claude Sonnet 4 sampling count/temperature and Agentless localization context on Verified-50. Outputs are agent trajectories and tests; no root-cause taxonomy or per-bug causal label is produced.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper data-availability statement links its replication package by citation; references provide exact GitHub URL. Public GitHub repository About title identifies ISSTA 2026 paper, and README explicitly describes itself as supplementary materials, points to Hugging Face trajectories, analysis scripts, raw results and experiment READMEs. Hugging Face dataset page is public, lists the same agent/model combinations, provides download instructions and reports 3.28 GB. GitHub archive comment pins commit 31251be42ca1aa3251890f7b1d1b678462fa1420. No root license file was present in repository snapshot; paper itself is CC BY 4.0.
source_commit_or_archive: GitHub codeload archive for ARiSE-Lab/understanding-apr-agents at commit 31251be42ca1aa3251890f7b1d1b678462fa1420; 33 MB; SHA-256 1c436709062954c3834b7226c17d9b4553f74bac44433a40853ea9b8a251b515. Static-inspected README, requirements.txt, reproducer-analysis scripts/README, reproduction-test-localization scripts/README, generate_reproduction_tests.py, localize.py and retrieve.py. No code was run. Hugging Face trajectory data are separately public (3.28 GB).
license: arXiv paper CC BY 4.0; no explicit top-level license found in the GitHub software/data repository or Hugging Face dataset card (card has missing/empty YAML metadata warning). Do not assume software/trace reuse terms beyond public access.
exact_models: Main trace comparisons: Claude-3.5-Sonnet (agent versions vary) and GPT-4o; combinations constrained by public trajectory availability.
LLM judge for patch clone classification and step annotation: Claude Sonnet 4.
Verified-50 test-generation/localization experiments: Claude Sonnet 4, with 15/40 samples and temperatures 0.2/0.6/1.0.
weights_status: Hosted commercial APIs; no open weights. Exact GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet snapshot/deployment pins are incomplete. README requires Anthropic/OpenAI keys for regeneration and exact localization experiments. No API calls made.
evaluation_route: Read all 13,613 words / 1,310 extracted lines of arXiv v3 in consecutive sections, including methods, four RQs, threats, conclusion and full references; SHA-256 94e7c0db3e6c139515fc7a1bb34e46e160f0d23908199f87c261b272226b9d27. Study analyzes 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 5 agents. Main findings include issue difficulty drop, agent-specific patch styles, low repro trigger rates, reproducer overfitting, and regression selection gaps. Reported test-generation experiment: Agentless reproducer success across 40 samples is 46.0% at t=.2 vs 42.7% at .6 and 42.3% at 1.0; adding localization raises 697/1500 vs 614/1500 successful tests (13.5% relative; improvements in 27/50 tasks). Public repo has code, tables, plots and results; HF traces are 3.28 GB. Most descriptive analyses can be recomputed from cached traces; new RQ3 model runs require API calls and external Agentless repository/container setup. No execution/reproduction.
blockers: Public artifact has substantive analysis code, output tables/figures, and public trace data, but GitHub repo has no explicit software license and Hugging Face dataset card is missing license metadata.

Exact full rerun of original traces requires commercial Claude-3.5-Sonnet/GPT-4o agent configurations and private/historic agent environments; many results are better analyzed from cached trajectories.

New reproducer/localization experiments require paid Claude Sonnet 4 API calls, Agentless repository located at a hard-coded author path in docs, SWE-bench Docker environments and large sampling (50 issues × 30/40 samples, plus six 15/40×temperature configurations). No calls made.

The trajectories are a 3.28 GB Hugging Face download; dataset viewer currently errors when inferring heterogeneous per-task result schemas. Raw files are public, but custom per-file parsing may be needed.
SWT-Bench is not the study benchmark; SWE-bench Verified is. This is agent process/test-validation analysis, not a Defects4J/BugsInPy method or ground-truth root-cause classifier.
concept_fit: Very high conceptual fit for issue-to-reproducing-test quality and diagnosis-informed testing: quantifies test generation, whether tests actually trigger issues, test-overfitting, regression test selection, and measures the effect of localization context. Directly supports a root-cause/reproducer-quality evaluation protocol. It does not define or classify root causes, and its core 500-task cohort is SWE-bench Verified rather than SWT-Bench.
recommendation: Promote as high-priority SWT-adjacent conceptual/protocol paper for evaluating bug-revealing tests and test-driven root-cause work. Public source plus 3.28 GB public trajectories make cached-behavior analysis substantially reproducible; its repo provides scripts and results. It is not a direct SWT-Bench dataset paper, and full re-generation requires paid GPT-4o/Claude APIs plus Agentless/Docker setup. First use cached trajectories and reproduce/test the analysis tables; use the 50-task localization/reproducer experiment only after separate API-budget approval. For the project’s own Qwen model, an independent evaluation would require adapting the API-bound generation driver, so not a zero-change model route. No code, API or reproduction run.
supporting_locations: Full text SHA-256 94e7c0db3e6c139515fc7a1bb34e46e160f0d23908199f87c261b272226b9d27; all 1,310 extracted lines / 13,613 words read, including complete references.
Sections 2–3: trajectory annotations, five agent architectures, SWE-bench Verified 500 tasks, agent/model configurations.
Sections 4–5: patch divergence, task difficulty, overlap, reproducer overfitting analysis.

Section 6: Agentless/SWE-Agent reproducer and regression selection; localization improves reproducer samples 614/1500→697/1500 on Verified-50; low-temperature 40-sample test generation 46.0% issue reproduction.
Sections 7–9 and conclusion: tooling study and limits; no ground-truth root-cause taxonomy, commercial API, subset/sample restrictions.

GitHub README and pinned archive contain analysis scripts, published tables/plots and raw results; requirement pins and exact experiment README inspected. Hugging Face card gives 3.28GB data, listed models and a dataset-viewer schema error.
